questions.question:
There are 3 triangles on a grid. Exactly 2 have the same area, exactly 2 are isosceles, and exactly 2 are right-angled. Two of the triangles are shown. Which could be the third?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

The large rectangle shown is made up of nine identical rectangles whose longest sides are $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ long. What is the perimeter of the large rectangle?
Choices:
A:$40 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$48 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$76 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$81 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$90 \mathrm{~cm}$
A rectangular strip of paper of dimensions $4 \times 13$ is folded as shown in the diagram. Two rectangles are formed with areas $P$ and $Q$ where $P=2 Q$. What is the value of $x$?

In the diagram, the small equilateral triangles have area $4 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. What is the area of the shaded region?
Choices:
A:$80 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
B:$90 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
C:$100 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
D:$110 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
E:$120 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$

Three congruent isosceles trapeziums are assembled to form an equilateral triangle with a hole in the middle, as shown in the diagram.
What is the perimeter of the hole?
Choices:
A:$3 a+6 b$
B:$3 b-6 a$
C:$6 b-3 a$
D:$6 a+3 b$
E:$6 a-3 b$

A square piece of paper of area $64 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ is folded twice, as shown in the diagram. What is the sum of the areas of the two shaded rectangles?
Choices:
A:$10 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
B:$14 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
C:$15 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
D:$16 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
E:$24 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$

A triangular piece of paper is folded along the dotted line shown in the left-hand diagram to form the heptagon shown in the right-hand diagram. The total area of the shaded parts of the heptagon is $1 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. The area of the original triangle is $1 \frac{1}{2}$ times the area of the heptagon. What is the area of the original triangle, in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$?

The diagram shows an octagon consisting of $10$ unit squares. The portion below $\overline{PQ}$ is a unit square and a triangle with base $5$. If $\overline{PQ}$ bisects the area of the octagon, what is the ratio $\frac{XQ}{QY}$?

Choices:
A:$\frac{2}{5}$
B:$\frac{1}{2}$
C:$\frac{3}{5}$
D:$\frac{2}{3}$
E:$\frac{3}{4}$

Which of the magnified sections cannot come from the picture shown?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

The rectangle $A B C D$ is made up of 12 congruent rectangles (see diagram). How big is the ratio $\frac{A D}{D C}$?
Choices:
A:$\frac{8}{9}$
B:$\frac{5}{6}$
C:$\frac{7}{8}$
D:$\frac{2}{3}$
E:$\frac{9}{8}$
The lengths of the sides of triangle $X Y Z$ are $X Z=\sqrt{55}$, $X Y=8, Y Z=9$. Find the length of the diagonal $X A$ of the rectangular parallelepiped in the figure.

Each of the five vases shown has the same height and each has a volume of 1 litre. Half a litre of water is poured into each vase. In which vase would the level of the water be the highest?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

The diagram on the right shows a solid made up of 6 triangles. Each vertex is assigned a number, two of which are indicated. The total of the three numbers on each triangle is the same. What is the total of all five numbers?

Three circular hoops are joined together so that they intersect at rightangles as shown. A path starts at an intersection and follows the outside of the hoops by repeating this procedure: travel along a quarter-circle, turn $90^{\circ}$ to the right, travel along a quarter-circle and turn $90^{\circ}$ to the left. How many quarter-circles does the path traverse before first returning to its starting point?

Three 12 cm $\times$ 12 cm squares are each cut into two pieces $A$ and $B$, as shown in the first figure below, by joining the midpoints of two adjacent sides.  These six pieces are then attached to a regular hexagon, as shown in the second figure, so as to fold into a polyhedron.  What is the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of this polyhedron?

The centers of the faces of the right rectangular prism shown below are joined to create an octahedron. What is the volume of the octahedron?

Choices:
A:$\frac{75}{12}$
B:$10$
C:$12$
D:$10\sqrt{2}$
E:$15$

Four identical rhombuses (diamonds) and two squares are fitted together to form a regular octagon as shown. How big are the obtuse interior angles in the rhombuses?
Choices:
A:$135^{\circ}$
B:$140^{\circ}$
C:$144^{\circ}$
D:$145^{\circ}$
E:$150^{\circ}$

Vases I, II and III contain 4 liters, 3 liters and 4 liters of water, respectively, as shown. Viewed from the front, the three vases appear to have the same size. Which of the following images could show the vases viewed from above?
Choices:
A:(A)
B:(B)
C:(C)
D:(D)
E:(E)

In a box-shaped water tank with dimensions $4 \mathrm{~m} \times 2 \mathrm{~m} \times 1 \mathrm{~m}$, the height of the water is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$. The tank is then turned on its side (see picture on the right). How high is the water in the tank now?
Choices:
A:$25 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$50 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$75 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$1 \mathrm{~m}$
E:$1.25 \mathrm{~m}$
Nine steps of a staircase arranged in a cylindrical order starting at the bottom and leading all the way to the top can be seen. All steps are equally high. How many steps cannot be seen?
